R-410A.name: R-410A (Puron)
R-410A.status: Being phased down under AIM Act. Available but decreasing production from 2025+.
R-410A.oilType: POE (Polyolester) - hygroscopic, absorbs moisture quickly. Keep sealed.
R-410A.chargingMethod: Must charge as liquid (blend - vapor charging changes composition).
serviceNotes: Always charge as liquid from tank - invert tank or use liquid port
Do NOT top off charge without finding leak first
POE oil absorbs moisture rapidly - minimize system open time
Requires 500 micron vacuum minimum - lower is better
Higher pressures than R-22 - use 800 psig rated hoses and gauges
replacements: R-32 (direct replacement in new equipment only)
R-454B (Opteon XL41 - approved drop-in for some equipment)

R-22.name: R-22 (HCFC-22, Freon)
R-22.status: BANNED from production/import since Jan 1, 2020. Only reclaimed/recycled available. Price has stabilized but remains high.
R-22.chargingMethod: Can charge as vapor or liquid.
serviceNotes: NO new R-22 production - use reclaimed only
Never mix R-22 with R-410A or other refrigerants
If system needs major repair, recommend R-410A system replacement (better long-term)
Drop-in replacements available (R-407C, R-422D, MO99) but have performance trade-offs
If converting to drop-in: change filter drier, check TXV compatibility, may need oil change

dropInReplacements.R-407C: Closest performance match. Requires POE oil change. TXV adjustment may be needed.
dropInReplacements.MO99 (R-438A): Can work with existing mineral oil in some cases. Check manufacturer approval.
dropInReplacements.R-422D: Easy retrofit but lower efficiency. Works with mineral oil.

R-32.name: R-32 (Difluoromethane)
R-32.status: The future standard. Used in Daikin Fit and many new mini-splits. Replacing R-410A globally.
R-32.chargingMethod: Single component - can charge as liquid or vapor.
serviceNotes: A2L classification - mildly flammable. No open flames during service.
Requires R-32 rated recovery machine and gauges
Electronic leak detectors must be rated for A2L
Same pressure range as R-410A - familiar working pressures
Higher efficiency than R-410A - 10% better COP
Lower charge weight than R-410A for same capacity
Single component - no composition shift, can top off charge (unlike R-410A)
safetyNotes: Burning velocity: 6.7 cm/s (very slow - won't explode but can ignite)
Do not use in enclosed spaces without ventilation
No brazing with refrigerant in system - standard practice applies
A2L rated equipment has safety features: leak sensors, charge limits per room volume

R-454B.name: R-454B (Opteon XL41)
R-454B.status: Approved as R-410A replacement. Carrier, Trane, Lennox developing R-454B equipment for 2025+ installations.
serviceNotes: Designed as near drop-in for R-410A equipment (NOT a retrofit for existing units)
New equipment factory-designed for R-454B
A2L safety requirements same as R-32
Must charge as liquid (blend)
Requires A2L rated tools and recovery equipment

R-407C.name: R-407C
R-407C.type: HFC zeotropic blend (23% R-32, 25% R-125, 52% R-134a)
R-407C.status: Used as primary R-22 retrofit refrigerant and in some commercial RTUs. Being phased down with other high-GWP HFCs under AIM Act.

operatingPressures.temperatureGlide: 10.5°F glide between bubble point and dew point — significant for charging and diagnostics

R-407C.oilType: POE (Polyolester) required — mineral oil incompatible with HFC blend
R-407C.chargingMethod: MUST charge as liquid only. Vapor charging causes fractionation — composition shifts, performance degrades permanently.
serviceNotes: Zeotropic blend with significant 10.5°F temperature glide — use bubble point for subcooling, dew point for superheat
Use PT chart specific to R-407C — has separate liquid and vapor saturation columns
After any leak, recover entire charge and recharge from new cylinder — cannot top off (composition has shifted)
POE oil required — if converting from R-22 system, flush mineral oil 3 times minimum or replace oil
Replace filter drier with POE-compatible drier when converting
TXV may need superheat adjustment after R-22 to R-407C retrofit
Higher discharge temps than R-22 — check compressor amp draw and discharge line temp
Handles like R-22 in terms of pressures, but composition and oil requirements are completely different

R-134a.name: R-134a (Tetrafluoroethane)
R-134a.status: Phased out of new automotive A/C in US (replaced by R-1234yf). Still used in commercial refrigeration, chillers, and some heat pump water heaters. Being phased down under AIM Act.

operatingPressures.suctionNormal: 20-30 psig at 95°F ambient (much lower than R-410A)

R-134a.oilType: POE (Polyolester) for stationary applications. PAG (Polyalkylene Glycol) for automotive A/C — NOT interchangeable with POE.
R-134a.chargingMethod: Single component — can charge as liquid or vapor. Most often charged by weight on commercial equipment.
serviceNotes: Common in TXV applications: chillers, walk-in coolers, transport refrigeration, vending machines, beverage coolers, dehumidifiers
Low pressures — do NOT use 800 psig R-410A gauges (poor resolution at low pressure). Use R-22/R-134a range gauges.
POE oil hygroscopic — same moisture precautions as R-410A
Vacuum to 500 microns minimum
Excellent at moderate-temp applications (35-50°F evaporator), poor at low-temp below 0°F
When working on automotive, use PAG-compatible tools — NEVER mix PAG and POE in same system
Being replaced by R-1234yf in new automotive and R-513A in some stationary applications

R-448A.name: R-448A (Solstice N40)
R-448A.status: Primary replacement for R-404A in commercial refrigeration. Widely used in supermarket and food service applications. EPA SNAP-approved for retrofit use.

operatingPressures.suctionNormal: Similar to R-404A: 25-40 psig low-temp, 50-75 psig medium-temp

R-448A.oilType: POE (Polyolester) — same as R-404A and R-410A
R-448A.chargingMethod: MUST charge as liquid (zeotropic blend). Recover entire charge after leak repair — cannot top off without composition shift.
serviceNotes: Drop-in replacement for R-404A in existing equipment with minor modifications
Lower GWP than R-404A (3922) by approximately 65%
Slightly higher discharge temperatures than R-404A — monitor compressor temp on retrofits
Use bubble point for subcooling calculations, dew point for superheat (glide refrigerant)
Replace filter drier when retrofitting R-404A systems
TXV adjustment usually needed — may need different orifice on systems with fixed metering devices
A1 classification — no flammability concerns, standard service practices apply

R-290.name: R-290 (Propane)
R-290.status: Approved by EPA SNAP for limited commercial refrigeration and small self-contained appliances. Charge limited to 150g under current US residential rules; some commercial categories allow up to 500g. BANNED in central A/C and split systems in US.
R-290.oilType: Mineral oil or POE (manufacturer specific) — propane is miscible with most refrigeration oils
R-290.chargingMethod: Single component — charge by weight only on factory-sealed systems. Most R-290 equipment is factory-charged and not field-serviceable for refrigerant addition.
serviceNotes: EXTREMELY FLAMMABLE — lower flammability limit 2.1%, ignition energy only 0.25 mJ (any spark can ignite)
Charge limit currently 150g residential / 500g some commercial categories under US EPA
ONLY work on R-290 equipment with manufacturer-specific training and intrinsically safe tools
Recovery requires explosion-proof recovery machine — standard machines are dangerous and illegal for A3 refrigerants
Leak detector must be rated for hydrocarbon gases — most A2L detectors are NOT rated for A3
No open flames, smoking, or ignition sources within 30 ft of service work
Ventilation mandatory — propane is heavier than air, accumulates at floor level in enclosed spaces
Highly efficient — 30% lower charge than HFCs for same cooling capacity
GWP only 3 — one of lowest of any refrigerant, environmentally excellent
bannedFrom: Central air conditioning (residential and commercial split systems)
Any system over 500g charge in US
Field-charged split systems (must be factory sealed with approved charge weight)

R-1234yf.name: R-1234yf (HFO-1234yf, Opteon YF)
R-1234yf.status: Standard refrigerant for new automotive A/C since 2017 (US and EU mandate). Growing in stationary HVAC as a blend component. Atmospheric lifetime only 11 days — essentially no global warming contribution.
R-1234yf.oilType: POE or PAG (automotive-specific PAG synthetic for OEM vehicle systems)
R-1234yf.chargingMethod: Single component — can charge as liquid or vapor. Automotive systems use dedicated A/C service machines that recover, evacuate, and weigh in charge automatically.
serviceNotes: Very low GWP (4) — one of most environmentally friendly synthetic refrigerants available
A2L mildly flammable — same handling precautions as R-32: no open flames, A2L-rated tools required
Burning velocity extremely slow (1.5 cm/s) — very difficult to ignite compared to propane
More expensive than R-134a (currently 5-10x cost per pound)
Pressures and operating characteristics very close to R-134a — similar gauge ranges work
Found as major component in HVAC blends: R-454B (31% R-1234yf), R-448A (21% R-1234yf)
Used in some commercial centrifugal chillers and stationary equipment
applications: Automotive A/C (2017+ vehicles in US and EU)
Component in HVAC blends (R-454B, R-448A, R-513A)

R-466A.name: R-466A
R-466A.type: HFC/HFO blend with iodotrifluoromethane (49% R-32, 11.5% R-125, 39.5% CF3I)
R-466A.classification: A1 (non-flammable, non-toxic) — primary advantage over R-32 and R-454B
R-466A.status: Under evaluation as non-flammable R-410A replacement. Being tested by Chemours and equipment manufacturers. Not yet widely deployed — regulatory approval and stability testing ongoing 2025-2026.

operatingPressures.suctionNormal: Similar to R-410A: 115-125 psig at 95°F ambient
operatingPressures.dischargeNormal: Similar to R-410A: 370-410 psig at 95°F ambient

R-466A.chargingMethod: Charge as liquid per manufacturer — very low glide makes it more forgiving than other zeotropes.
serviceNotes: PRIMARY VALUE: A1 classification means NO flammability concerns — existing service practices, no A2L tooling required
GWP 733 — significantly lower than R-410A (2088) but higher than R-32 (675) or R-454B (466)
Contains CF3I (trifluoroiodomethane) — novel iodine-containing molecule with some light sensitivity questions
Pressures, oil, and capacity nearly identical to R-410A — smooth transition for technicians already familiar
Stability under high temperatures and UV exposure being studied — long-term field data still developing
Currently more expensive than A2L alternatives — market adoption depends on cost parity
Best fit for applications where A2L flammability is a code concern (older buildings, specific jurisdictions)
Drop-in potential for existing R-410A equipment under evaluation — not yet manufacturer-approved as retrofit
